operation_details.item: The user avoids all caffeine by lifelong personal choice due to anxiety and sleep disruption.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: How's your latest article coming along? I imagine you've been deep in the editing flow today.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: It's going well, but I keep hitting an afternoon lull. I need to find a way to stay sharp without relying on stimulants.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That's a real challenge for writers. Many people reach for a coffee or tea at this hour. Have you ever tried that?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: I avoid all caffeine as a lifelong personal choice because it worsens my anxiety and disrupts my sleep; I do not drink coffee, tea, energy drinks, or caffeinated soda.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Thank you for sharing that — it's completely understandable. I'm not a medical professional, but it sounds like you've built a routine that respects your body's needs. Herbal tea, plain water, or even a short walk could be gentle ways to refresh.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: I'm pulling a late night to finish an article. What should I drink to stay focused?

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: For a late-night session, I'd suggest something caffeine-free like a mild herbal tea — peppermint can be refreshing, while chamomile is calming. Also keep a glass of water nearby. And don't forget to take a few short breaks and get proper rest, since your brain will work better after a real break.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Chamomile sounds nice, actually. I'll brew a cup and set a timer for a quick stretch break too.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That's a solid plan. Gentle hydration and movement can keep your mind clearer than any stimulant, especially when you're working late. I hope the article flows well.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Thanks for the support. I'll let you know how it goes when it's published.
